newsitem.title: UK: UK gilt futures edge higher, await data.
newsitem.headline: UK gilt futures edge higher, await data.

text.p: UK gilt futures edged higher at the opening but slipped back in early dealings as the market awaited manufacturing output and producer price data at 0830 GMT.
The September contract started 3/32 higher at 114-05/32 but soon eased back to 114-02.
Comments from EU finance ministers that EMU would start on time in 1999 supported Bunds, but traders said gilts looked vulnerable to profit-taking at current levels.
"The UK, with its opt-out, is really standing aside from this," said Andrew Davies of London Bond Broking.
April manufacturing output is expected to show a rebound after a dip the previous month while May PPIs are expected to show pipeline price pressures flat.
"I don't think the data are going to be particularly positive for gilts," said Tom Rayner of Societe Generale.
Davies noted that after Friday's quarter-point rise in UK rates to 6.50 percent, short-dated gilts were little changed to a touch easier while long gilts were quite firm.
"As a result of that, the terms for taking more defensive positions in the market are more attractive today than they were on Friday. That might encourage a little bit of profit-taking."
The gilt-Bund 10-year spread widened to 142 basis points from 139 on Friday.
September short sterling was down one basis point at 93.13, implying official interest rates around 6.85 percent at the end of the third quarter.
